title: ClearView Medical - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for implementation of Redwood inference platform for ClearView Medical. Covered onboarding timeline, access & SSO, security requirements (SOC2/KMS), test plan for pilot, success criteria, and next steps (share onboarding checklist, schedule technical deep dive, start staging access).
topics: Security & compliance requirements (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs)
Environment setup: staging vs production, VPC/private deployment options
Pilot scope: tests, traffic profile, success criteria
action_items: Jordan Kim: Send onboarding checklist & deployment playbook (link) by 2025-12-11
Samir Gupta: Share staging network diagram and initial infra requirements by 2025-12-12
Riley Chen: Create project in Redwood Console and invite ClearView team (Maya, Ethan) by 2025-12-10
Priya Nair (ClearView): Provide SSO metadata and required IP allowlist details by 2025-12-12
Ethan Park (ClearView): Share representative traffic samples and success metrics doc by 2025-12-15
next_steps: Redwood to provision staging tenant and invite customer users
Schedule technical deep-dive (SE-led) focused on Private deployment options and network setup
Customer to share compliance questionnaire and KMS requirements
Coordinate dates for a 2-week pilot starting late Jan (target)
transcript:
Header: 
Date: 2025-12-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Riley Chen (Redwood CSM), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (ClearView Head of AI), Ethan Park (Eng Manager), Priya Nair (Security), Liam O'Connor (Product)

[00:00] Jordan Kim: All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is Jordan from Redwood, i'll kick us off. um, quick round of intros — real quick — and then we'll walk through the onboarding plan and next steps. Riley, wanna say hi?

[00:10] Riley Chen: Hi all, Riley here, I'm your CSM; i'll be the day-to-day contact for rollout and adoption stuff. excited to work with the ClearView team.

[00:18] Maya Lopez: Hi, Maya here. I'm leading the AI program at ClearView. we're looking to replace a batch of in-house inference pods with a more predictable production runtime. main concerns: latency for clinical workflows, and data residency, and obviously security.

[00:32] Samir Gupta: hey team, Samir, SE on the Redwood side. i'll be helping with infra design, benchmarks, and the pilot.

[00:40] Ethan Park: Ethan, engineering manager. i'll own the integration points and making sure the CI/CD pipelines can push to staging.

[00:48] Priya Nair: Priya from security, i'll be validating SOC 2 stuff, key management and network controls.

[00:56] Jordan Kim: Great, thanks. quick agenda: 1) timeline and milestones, 2) access & SSO, 3) security/compliance items, 4) pilot scope & success criteria, 5) immediate next steps.

[01:10] Jordan Kim: On timeline, our recommendation is: provision staging tenant this week, config SSO + RBAC next week, run integration and baseline benchmarks in mid-December, then plan a 2-week pilot in late Jan. is that aligned with your timelines? Maya?

[01:28] Maya Lopez: that sounds reasonable. we have a Q1 product launch, so late Jan pilot fits. we do need to lock down data residency and whether we do private deployment vs dedicated first.

[01:41] Samir Gupta: quick note on that — for regulated workloads you can either go Redwood Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) depending on residency. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and isolation, Private gives you customer-managed network and KMS. we can scope both but pilot typically starts on staging hosted tenant to validate functionality.

[02:05] Priya Nair: What about KMS integration — we need HSM support or at least BYOK with our cloud KMS.

[02:13] Samir Gupta: yes we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (BYOK), and we have HSM compatibility on the Private option. i'll document exact KMS modes — there are a couple of patterns depending on Dedicated vs Private.

[02:30] Jordan Kim: i'll also share the security pack with SOC 2 controls and encryption in transit and at rest notes.

[02:36] Ethan Park: on the integration side, our main flow is a REST API call from our backend. what's the auth pattern for Redwood?

[02:44] Riley Chen: you'll get API keys for dev/staging; for production we recommend SSO + role-based access and short-lived credentials; we can also integrate with your SAML SSO.

[02:56] Ethan Park: okay, good. and any network requirements? we run in GCP with a strict egress policy.

[03:04] Samir Gupta: for hosted staging, we can provide IP ranges to allowlist; for Private deployments we'll need VPC peering or private link depending on your cloud. i'll share the diagram.

[03:18] Maya Lopez: can we also do a perf baseline? tokens per second, latency p50/p95 under our real prompts.

[03:26] Samir Gupta: yes, absolutely. please share representative prompts and traffic patterns. we'll run baseline benchmarks and share a spreadsheet with token counts, latency, and cost estimates.

[03:40] Jordan Kim: action items: we'll send onboarding checklist and playbook, Samir will share infra diagram, Riley will invite the team to the Console. Priya, please send SSO metadata and allowlist.

[03:52] Priya Nair: sure, i'll get that over — small note, we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, is that supported?

[03:59] Samir Gupta: yes, audit logs and request traces can be exported; we have integrations and also can ship logs to S3/BigQuery depending on your stack.

[04:10] Liam O'Connor: a couple quick product questions: how easy is it to pin a model version and do canary rollouts?

[04:17] Samir Gupta: the Console supports model pinning and rollout policies — canary, A/B, automatic fallback. we can demo that in the next session.

[04:26] Maya Lopez: also cost question — how do we estimate per-token cost for the pilot?

[04:31] Jordan Kim: we'll provide a cost estimation sheet after we see the sample traffic. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and quantization configs to reduce unit cost.

[04:42] Ethan Park: regarding compliance questionnaire — we'll need Redwood to fill out our security questionnaire for procurement.

[04:48] Riley Chen: absolutely, i'll attach the security pack and fill out the questionnaire; also we can set up a SOC 2/ISO documentation share.

[05:00] Priya Nair: what's the expected escalation path if we hit an incident during the pilot?

[05:06] Riley Chen: CSM first-line, SE second, and AE/Eng escalation for SLA issues. for Dedicated/Private we can enable premium support. i'll add the support contacts to the project.

[05:18] Maya Lopez: sounds good. are there any blockers you foresee on your side to start staging?

[05:24] Samir Gupta: not really; we just need SSO metadata and network allowlist. if you prefer, we can do a short network kick-off with your infra team.

[05:34] Ethan Park: let's schedule that — i'll block a 30-minute session next week.

[05:39] Jordan Kim: excellent. quick recap of next steps and owners... (recap) Jordan to share onboarding link and schedule, Samir to send infra diagram, Riley to create project and invite, Priya to send SSO metadata and allowlist, Ethan to share traffic samples.

[05:58] Jordan Kim: any risks or escalations we should note?

[06:02] Priya Nair: only that we'll need legal review of data residency and any PHI handling. procurement will review the contract — timeline may slip if legal has follow-ups.

[06:12] Maya Lopez: also want to validate that audit logs and data retention policies meet our policies.

[06:18] Riley Chen: we'll include retention settings and log export options in the security pack.

[06:24] Jordan Kim: final note: we'll plan the technical deep-dive (SE-led) next week to walk through network, KMS, and pilot test plan. i'll send calendar invites after the call.

[06:35] Ethan Park: thanks everyone, that was helpful.

[06:38] Maya Lopez: thanks — looking forward.

[06:40] Jordan Kim: thanks all, we'll follow up with the items.

End of transcript.
